summary.text: Jessica Killin is the Democratic nominee for Colorado's 5th Congressional District. A Colorado Springs native and U.S. Army veteran with a Georgetown law degree, she worked at USAA and as a congressional and White House staffer, including as chief of staff to Second Gentleman Doug Emhoff. She describes her campaign as focused on affordability, anti-corruption measures and veterans' care.

paragraphs.text: Killin grew up on the east side of Colorado Springs, the child of a public school educator, and graduated from Falcon High School, according to her Ballotpedia survey.

She earned an ROTC scholarship and served in the U.S. Army as a Captain and paratrooper and as a Military Police Officer, per her Ballotpedia survey; the Colorado Sun reports she served from 1995 to 2003, including peacekeeping deployments in the Balkans.
She later earned a law degree from Georgetown University.
Killin spent over a decade at USAA, according to her Ballotpedia survey; the Colorado Sun reports she worked as a lobbyist for the company.

She then worked as chief of staff to Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and to then-Reps. Carolyn Maloney and Donna Shalala, and as an aide to then-Sens. Bill Nelson and Tom Carper, according to the Colorado Sun.
In 2023 she joined Second Gentleman Doug Emhoff's office as chief of staff, with a White House title that included deputy assistant to the President, per the Colorado Sun.
Killin returned to the 5th District in June 2025 and launched her campaign, according to the Colorado Sun.
She won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary over Joe Reagan, 61.2% to 38.8%.
She describes herself as a mother in a blended family with her husband, Raj, and three children.
